questions.q: How do you reach your personal Settings, per this lesson?
options: Click your profile photo in the top right, then choose Settings
Click the gear icon and choose Setup
There is no way to access personal settings in Salesforce
Only an admin can open another user's Settings for them
questions.explain: Personal Settings is reached from the profile photo menu, deliberately separate from the gear icon that opens Setup.

questions.q: What does this lesson say the Language & Time Zone setting controls?
options: How dates, numbers, and field labels render specifically for the logged-in user
Which objects exist in the org
Which users have System Administrator access
The org's billing currency for every user
questions.explain: Language & Time Zone is a personal setting that controls rendering for that specific user, independent of other users.

questions.q: If you're locked out of your own account, what does this lesson say is the self-service fix?
options: Click "Forgot Your Password?" on the login screen and enter your username to get a reset link by email
Call Salesforce support and request a new account
Ask any other user to reset it from their own Settings
There is no self-service option; an admin is always required
questions.explain: The "Forgot Your Password?" link on the login screen lets a user reset their own password without admin involvement.

questions.q: If a teammate (not you) is locked out of their account, what does this lesson say an admin should do?
options: Go to Setup → Users, select that person, and click Reset Password(s)
Log in as that person using their saved password
Delete and recreate the user's account from scratch
Nothing can be done until the user resets it themselves
questions.explain: An admin resets another user's password through Setup → Users → Reset Password(s), which requires admin permissions.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say resetting someone else's password lives in Setup, not in personal Settings?
options: Because it's an admin action performed on someone else's account, requiring permissions an ordinary user doesn't have
Because personal Settings cannot store passwords at all
Because Setup and personal Settings are actually the exact same menu
Because only Trailhead accounts support password resets
questions.explain: Resetting another user's password is an admin-level action on someone else's account, which is why it requires Setup access rather than living in personal Settings.
